title: Large Language Model-driven Meta-structure Discovery in Heterogeneous Information Network

problem.claim: Automatically discovering useful meta-structures in heterogeneous information networks is challenging because hand-crafted structures do not scale.

gap.claim: Prior search methods emphasized empirical performance while overlooking human comprehensibility and generalizability.

contributions.claim: ReStruct integrates large language model reasoning into an evolutionary meta-structure search procedure.

ReStruct combines grammar-based natural-language encoding and semantic-feasibility evaluation with performance-oriented evolutionary operations to jointly optimize explainability and empirical performance.
ReStruct includes a differential LLM explainer that generates and refines explanations for discovered meta-structures using search history.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight representative HIN datasets reportedly show state-of-the-art performance in recommendation and node classification tasks.
A survey of 73 graduate students reportedly found that ReStruct's discovered meta-structures and generated explanations were substantially more comprehensible.
The authors report that code and the questionnaire are publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heterogeneous information networks capture complex relations among diverse node types, and meta-structures are used to identify important patterns.
Existing automatic searches prioritized empirical performance over comprehensibility and generalizability.
ReStruct incorporates LLM reasoning, natural-language grammar translation, semantic evaluation, and performance-oriented evolutionary operations.
A differential LLM explainer generates and refines explanations from search history.
The abstract reports performance results across eight datasets and improved comprehensibility in a 73-student survey.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines semantic-feasibility evaluation with performance-oriented evolutionary operations.

interpretation.claim: Optimizing task performance together with human interpretability can address a limitation of performance-only search.

application.claim: For structure-discovery systems, represent candidates in a form that supports both automated performance evaluation and semantic review.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this joint objective is beneficial outside the reported HIN recommendation and node-classification settings.

source_observation.claim: The system generates and refines explanations by reasoning through search history.

interpretation.claim: Search history can provide context for producing explanations of discovered structures.

application.claim: Explanation components for iterative discovery systems can use prior search states to refine descriptions of selected results.

exception.claim: The abstract does not describe the explanation-generation procedure or evaluate explanation accuracy.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evolutionary operators, grammar, or LLM configurations.
The abstract does not report dataset names, baselines, metrics, or quantitative result values.
The abstract does not detail the survey protocol or comprehensibility measures.
The abstract does not establish generalizability beyond the reported datasets and tasks.
